    The indecomposable representations of the linear quiver #

    Consequences of the structure theorem and of the morphism computations:

    • intervals are indecomposable (indecomposable_interval) and isomorphic intervals have the same endpoints (interval_iso_iff);
    • every indecomposable representation is isomorphic to an interval (exists_iso_interval_of_indecomposable), so the intervals M_{a,d}, a ≤ d, form a complete set of representatives of the indecomposables, as stated after Definition 5.1;
    • (5.1): a monomorphism M_{a',d'} ⟶ M_{a,d} forces d' = d and a ≤ a', an epimorphism M_{a,d} ⟶ M_{a',d'} forces a' = a and d' ≤ d.

    Coordinates of compositions, identities and zero #

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.coord_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {c d a b a' b' : Fin n} (η : interval k c d ⟶ interval k a b) (θ : interval k a b ⟶ interval k a' b') (i : Fin n) :
    coord (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp η θ) i = coord η i * coord θ i
    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.coord_id {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} (a d i : Fin n) :
    coord (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (interval k a d)) i = if a ≤ i ∧ i ≤ d then 1 else 0
    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.coord_zero {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} (c d a b i : Fin n) :
    coord 0 i = 0

    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.coord_end_eq {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {a d : Fin n} (had : a ≤ d) (p : interval k a d ⟶ interval k a d) (i : Fin n) :
    coord p i = coord p a * coord (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (interval k a d)) i

    Isomorphic intervals have the same endpoints #

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.finrank_obj_eq_of_iso {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {X Y : Statement.LinRep k n} (e : X ≅ Y) (i : Fin n) :
    Module.finrank k ↑(X.obj i) = Module.finrank k ↑(Y.obj i)

    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.interval_iso_iff {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {a d a' d' : Fin n} (had : a ≤ d) (had' : a' ≤ d') :
    Nonempty (interval k a d ≅ interval k a' d') ↔ a = a' ∧ d = d'

    Indecomposables are intervals #

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.exists_iso_interval_of_indecomposable {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {X : Statement.LinRep k n} (hX : CategoryTheory.Indecomposable X) :
    ∃ (a : Fin n) (d : Fin n), a ≤ d ∧ Nonempty (X ≅ interval k a d)

    Monomorphisms and epimorphisms between intervals (5.1) #

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.le_of_coord_ne_zero {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {c d a b : Fin n} (η : interval k c d ⟶ interval k a b) {i : Fin n} (h : coord η i ≠ 0) :
    a ≤ c ∧ b ≤ d

    A morphism between intervals with a nonzero coordinate forces the inequalities a ≤ c and b ≤ d.

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.eq_and_le_of_mono {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {a' d' a d : Fin n} (had' : a' ≤ d') (η : interval k a' d' ⟶ interval k a d) [CategoryTheory.Mono η] :
    d' = d ∧ a ≤ a'

    A monomorphism M_{a',d'} ⟶ M_{a,d} between nonzero intervals has d' = d and a ≤ a'.

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.eq_and_le_of_epi {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {a d a' d' : Fin n} (had' : a' ≤ d') (η : interval k a d ⟶ interval k a' d') [CategoryTheory.Epi η] :
    a' = a ∧ d' ≤ d

    An epimorphism M_{a,d} ⟶ M_{a',d'} between nonzero intervals has a' = a and d' ≤ d.
